### Added
- **`plan_approval.py --status` reads an approval's standing and writes nothing.** It answers by the gate's own check: `holds`, `reason`, the recorded and current plan hash, and `drifted`, the files that moved since. Exit 0 when it holds, 1 when not. A write now prints the verdict, plan hash, file count and artifact path; `--json` prints the whole record. Before, every write printed both hashes of every file: about 20 KB for a plan with 130 reference files.
- **A plan section's body can live in a reference file.** A line under the heading that reads `→ [refs/x.md](../refs/x.md)` is a pointer: `## Related Code Files` in a phase file and `## Red-team disposition` in plan.md are read from the file it points to. Before, the approval refused APPROVED once the disposition table moved to `refs/`. Only an arrow line is a pointer, and only to a markdown file the approval hash pins (plan.md, a phase file, a file under a reference dir) other than its own.
- **`redteam_disposition.py` rewrites disposition cites.** `--pin-cites` follows every unquoted plan-local cite with a «quote» of its line, so a later move is caught by content; a table-row line is quoted by its cells, in order. `--remap-cites --from <git rev or old plan dir>` moves each of this plan's cites to where its old lines stand now and quotes it; another plan's cite is left alone. The old file is aligned with today's, read through its pointers, so a blank line, a table separator or a fence line is placed by its neighbours, and a cite into a file that did not change, `plan-graph.yaml` included, keeps its place. A cite that cannot be placed exactly once is left as it is and named; a bare `:N` after a cite that moved is written with the file it always meant. Only the lines read as the table are rewritten. `--plan` takes the plan's dir or its name, and the cite warnings print the runnable command.
- **An empty disposition table read through a pointer names the file read.** The refusal says `refs/x.md (through the pointer at plan.md:N) has no rows`, not plan.md.
- **`hs-rops fetch --print` / `--grep PAT` / `--lane NAME` — read a lane file where it lies.** `--grep` prints the matching lines with their numbers and exits 1 when none matches; `--print` prints the whole file. `--lane` names the dir a relative path is under. None of them checks, syncs or builds a tree, so a previous run's log can still be read after another local commit has moved HEAD. Before, the only way was `run --stale-ok`, which means measuring the old tree.
- **`hs-rops run --lock NAME` (and `ROPS_LOCK`) — a machine-wide named lock.** Runs that hold the same name take turns for the command's whole life. Use it for what no lane dir or `ROPS_LOCK_ENV` covers, such as two full suites that must not share the CPU. The flag is repeatable and also works on every `ROPS_CMD_*` alias. Names are taken in sorted order, so two runs naming them in opposite orders cannot deadlock.
- **`hs-rops` prints `[rops] exit_code=N` on stderr after its envelope.** A line filter that drops JSON envelope lines no longer drops the exit code with them. It is the last line even when stdout and stderr share one pipe.
- **`ROPS_LANE_SETUP` — a lane runs the setup its repo declares.** On every `lane` build or rebuild (so also on a `run --lane` that rebuilds), the command runs in the lane after its sync, with `ROPS_ENV` exported. Use it for creating the database the lane's env names, for example. It prints `setup: rc=0`, and a failure fails the build, naming the key.
- **`decision_register.py --amend DEC-n --title/--rationale` — reword a live ruling.** Runs inside the register lock. The ruling keeps the actor and ts of whoever made it. The replaced text is appended to `docs/decision-revisions.jsonl`, then `docs/decisions.md` is re-rendered, and the output names the three files to commit together. A superseded ruling is refused.
- **`hs-run cook next` answers `phase_paused`.** When the phase named by `--phase` is paused, or waits on a paused phase, the envelope carries `held_by`, `paused_reason` and `reopen_when`. This replaces the build or verify state the phase would otherwise report. `reopen_when` is never run. An `ask_user` block offers: lift the pause, or leave it parked.
- **`reference_dirs:` in plan.md — the approval hash covers the plan's reference files.** Files under the plan's `refs/` (default) or the dirs plan.md names are hashed with the plan and phase files, and scanned for `TBD`. A dir outside the plan, `.`, or `artifacts/` refuses approval. Approval warns, once, about plan-dir files a phase links to that the hash does not cover.
- **`hs-code check pkgsync` reads each package's tests.** A dependency only the tests import is the new law `test_only` ("move it to a test group"), not `stale`; test imports count as use for `[project.optional-dependencies]` / `[dependency-groups]`. A test file that does not parse is a warning, not a crash.
- **Runs on one lane take turns.** Every remote command holds a lock on its resolved remote dir, and on the values of the `ROPS_ENV` names listed in `ROPS_LOCK_ENV` (a DB URL, which a `run --at` worktree shares with its lane). The waiting run prints who holds it (names, never values) and gives up after `ROPS_LOCK_WAIT` (1800 s) with rc 75. A lane rebuild waits the same way before it rewrites the tree; `--at` names the env it shares.
- **`hs-code graph grep` — a string search that tells a use from a mention.** Every git-tracked file, one row per match, typed by where it sits: `code` / `docstring` / `comment` / `string` in `.py` (with the enclosing def or class), `data` with its key path in YAML/TOML/JSON (a suffixless JSON file such as `.test_durations` included), `doc` with its heading path and fence in Markdown, else `text`. Counts per kind cover every match; `--kind`, `--top`, `-i`. Measured on a 147-dist workspace: a name a research note called "where it is computed" was a module docstring.
- **Facts `code.mentions` and `code.stale_mentions`.** The first answers where a named subject is still written (plan `needs_planner`, same `--fact-subjects` as `code.callers`); a live symbol's `code` hits are counted only, since the graph facts list them, and anything else (an env name, a key) lists every kind. The second names what the diff removed and where it is still written (review, fix): the docstring or config key that outlives what it named. At most 20 rows per subject.
- **`hs-code change impact --data-key KEY`** — a data key or enum value (or a JSON pointer to one) has no symbol, so its blast radius is that of the code reading it by name: where it is declared (YAML/TOML/JSON), the symbols reading it, reads outside any symbol, and their radius over the working tree. A key no tracked file mentions exits 1.
- **`cook next` names the phases ready alongside the one it answers for** (`ready_alongside`, plus a warning carrying each one's `--phase` command), so a parallel lane is not left to reading the plan graph.
- **`graph where` matches a method by its bare name** (`^corrections_for$` finds `PgCorrections.corrections_for`). `hs:debug` and `hs:scout` point at `graph grep`.

- **`HARNESS_PYTHON` picks the interpreter every launcher runs under** — a path or a command prefix (`uv run --no-project --python 3.14 --with-requirements <harness>/requirements-runtime.txt python`). A repo whose syntax the `python3` on PATH cannot parse (`except A, B:` under 3.12) can now snapshot, and the `facts_stale` refresh command runs as printed. The `UNPARSEABLE` hint names the knob.
- **`harness/requirements-runtime.txt`** — the REQUIRED tier of `requirements.txt`, generated (`preflight_deps.py --write-runtime`) and held to it by a test: the recipe above no longer fetches every OPTIONAL dev tool (one such fetch failing behind a TLS-intercepting proxy sank the launcher).
- **`graph tests` lists what it counts**: `orphan_paths` (unit level) and `blind_func_ids` (function level), cut by `--top`; the counts stay totals.
- **`scaffold new-dist`/`new-module` work on a codemap with no `scaffold.templates`** (the shape `hs:codemap` writes; both verbs refused there). A dist is read off an existing dist declaring the same `[tool.<namespace_root>] tier`, closest name family first; a module lands in its parent package's directory. Every inference is a `warnings` line; `--module` overrides the derived import path. A codemap that does declare templates keeps the old contract.

- **`hs-rops run --at <rev>` and `run --sync`.** `--at` runs in a throwaway clean worktree of one commit, removed afterwards even on failure, timeout or a signal; `--sync` brings the remote tree up to date first (on `run` and every alias).
- **`hs-code check dist-obligations <dist>|--all`** reports which repo registries a dist is missing from, off a codemap `obligations:` block; `new-dist` names what the new dist owes. **`check pkgsync --dist`** keeps one package's rows.
- **codemap `copies:`** declares generated and backup trees; `graph grep` skips them by default, counts them, and `--include-copies` reads them.
- **`change test select` reaches the tests a data file or a doc can redden**: a test whose literals name the changed path or its directory (`string`), and codemap `test_select:` rows of `kind: whole_tree`. `code.tests_reached` reads the same channels.
- **`scaffold new-dist` renders the per-dist docs the repo declares** (`scaffold.templates` `kind: dist-doc`: a source section, or a link such as `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md`).
- **A repo routes its own rules into cook** through `.harness/cook-rules.yaml`, keyed by globs of what a phase creates.
- **`glossary_register --update --term`** revises a term and appends a revision trail; every register runs a repo-declared command (`docs/registers.yaml`) after a write.
- **`graph importers` answers for a package** (submodules included, each row names the module it goes through; `--exact` asks for the package module alone) and for a unique name tail. `graph where --symbol` takes the pattern as a flag.

- **A check keeps its real name under a canonical type: `<type>/<name>`.** `cook verify --check lint/ruff:PASS --check typecheck/mypy:PASS` is accepted: the part before `/` is one of test-policy's `test_types`, which now include `lint` (sarif) and `typecheck` (junit), and the name is free. Before, a ruff or mypy result had to be recorded as `unit` or `integration` to get past the name advisory. The DoD gate reads every check of a required type (`unit/core`, `unit/plugins`), and all of them must pass. A first phase snapshot written under the soft name check with names outside `test_types` now yields to a re-verify whose every name is known; the replaced record goes to `phase-superseded-<phase>.jsonl`. Both the name check and that yield read the test-policy of the project that owns the plan, as the DoD gate does.

### Fixed
- **`cook next --phase` on a paused phase says paused when every other phase passed.** With the rest of the plan passed, the plan read complete and the paused phase fell through to the plan's final review, `needs_review`, sized by the whole branch's diff, for a phase with no commit of its own. A paused phase named by `--phase` now answers `phase_paused` with its reason and reopen condition before completion is read; an unforced `next` still answers the plan's own next step. A plan whose frontmatter says completed over unfinished work still answers `state_conflict` first, whichever phase is named.
- **`cook verify --sha` no longer sizes the review below HEAD.** The run's review bracket ended at the first commit `--sha` named, so naming the open-mark commit after 600 lines of work measured 0 lines and waived the review. A `--sha` verify record now keeps the HEAD it was written at, and the gate sizes the run to both ends; either one over a threshold makes the review mandatory.
- **A tier-1 test-policy override keeps the shipped check types.** An override replaces the shipped file, so one written before `lint` and `typecheck` existed read `--check lint/ruff` as an unknown name, and the advisory then offered `lint/ruff` as the right form. A type an override leaves out now reads from the shipped default, the per-key union tier-2 already got; the override's own entry wins, and what a change must run is still its call. The advisory's examples come from the types the loaded policy accepts.
- **`cook verify --sha` checks every commit named.** A repeated `--sha` kept only its last value, so a refusal named one commit per run; every value now counts. A named commit on the first-parent line of a branch that does not hold HEAD (the base the phase branch was cut from, or the phase's own work taken there by fast-forward) is recorded with a warning that names the branch. A commit another branch holds only through a merge is this line's own and is not warned about.
- **A disposition cite followed by `of <doc>` or `của <doc>` names another document.** `--remap-cites` no longer moves it onto this plan's line of the same number, and `hs-run plan next` counts it as `foreign` instead of checking it against the file named before it; a bare `:N` after it in the cell means that document too.
- **`hs-run review next --range <commit>|<A..B>` briefs a review of committed work.** `changed_files` come from `git diff <range>`, and the bundle carries `range`. On a clean working tree, `nothing_changed` now says it read the working tree only and warns about commits the upstream does not hold.
- **`cook verify --sha` refuses commits that are not the branch's own work.** A merge commit, or a commit off HEAD's first-parent line (one that came in through a merge), is refused and nothing is recorded; the refusal names them and the `git rev-list --first-parent --no-merges <start>..HEAD` that lists the phase's own. Before, a `git log` range without `--first-parent` recorded about 125 merged-in commits with no word. A named commit another branch already holds is recorded with a warning. Commas or whitespace separate the names. Each `verify` line in `phase-commits.jsonl` now names, as `supersedes`, the `ts` of the phase's line it replaces.
- **`code.callers` no longer reads a method called through an instance as uncalled.** The snapshot never resolves `obj.method()` when the receiver's type is unknown, so such a method answered `[]`. For a method subject, every `.<name>` use in the measured files is now listed under `unresolved`, with its receivers; string literals comments and import statements are skipped, and a receiver on an earlier line (or before a backslash continuation) still counts. These uses are candidates by name, never mixed into `value`. At most 20 files are listed per subject, each with its `uses` count and at most 20 lines; a per-subject warning counts them all, and the facts size ceiling trims them before any value.
- **`hs-run cook verify` says what its exit 11 means.** After a recorded verification, `next_action` states that the write is done and that exit 11 means one deterministic step is left, not a failure. It also names that step, which is `next_command` too.
- **A register's post-write command: the files it changes join `commit_together`.** The repo declares the command, so nothing knows in advance which files it writes. The working tree is measured with git just before and just after it runs. Every path whose bytes moved is reported as `post_write.changed` and added to the `commit_together` list the write already named. Before, `--amend` re-rendered a page that the list left out.
- **`hs-run cook next` carries the preflight's warnings.** On an approved plan, `needs_open` used to answer `warnings: []`, so the `../<sibling-plan>/` spelling for an evidence citation showed only under `cook preflight`. `preflight_blocked` now lists the advisories after its reasons.
- **The held-commit warning of `cook verify` stays short.** It names at most five commits and three branches per commit, then how many more, and points to `git branch --contains`. Before, it spelled out every branch and could run to thousands of characters.
- **`hs-run test` names a recorded failure's failed checks.** `failed_checks` read a key no writer sets and was always a list of `null`; it now lists each failed check's name.
- **`hs-rops lane` no longer reports a code-less editable dist as hookless.** A meta dist whose dir holds only a pyproject and docs has nothing to hook, but it was reported as still lacking an import hook on every build. Such a dist is now skipped. A dist whose source dir does not exist is still reported. The walk visits dirs cheapest first: a dir costs its parent's cost, plus one, plus its rank among its sibling dirs, so neither a wide nor a deep data dir next to the code dir is walked through before it. A dir past 5000 entries is cut short; the walk reads at most 5000 dirs and 200000 entries, and the probe stops walking after 60 seconds, inside its 120-second timeout. A walk that ends without finding code but did not see everything (a budget or the deadline ran out, a dir was cut short, or a dir or entry could not be read) prints `walk-incomplete NAME`; that dist is named but not reinstalled.
- **`cook verify --phase P` names `cook next --plan … --phase P` as its next step.** The unforced `next` it used to name, when run in a worktree, handed out and marked whichever phase was free.
- **A re-verified phase keeps its whole latest record.** `phase-latest-<phase>.json` now holds the full latest record, on both the script path and the Write-tool path. `verification-<phase>.json` still keeps the first record that counted the phase. `cook verify` no longer swallows the advisory that a re-verify did not reach the snapshot, and it names the latest record's path.
- **A snapshot refusal names both ways out.** A missing codegraph store now names `--fresh` and `graph snapshot --apply`. A stale or mismatched snapshot names the store path that `--fresh` files into, which is never a tracked file.
- **`cook verify` leaves out commits another local branch already holds.** An open mark older than the base a phase branch was cut from used to count the base's own commits. They are now named in a warning, with their branch, and the warning points at `--sha`. A branch whose history holds HEAD (the branch a detached worktree sits on, or one the phase's work was already merged into) is still this tree's line.
- **An evidence path from a sibling plan is checked.** A `../<plan>/…` citation used to bypass the path pattern entirely. It is now followed from the plan dir and must exist inside the repo. A bare citation that only a sibling plan holds warns instead of blocking the preflight, and names the spelling that resolves.
- **`hs-rops run --timeout` help says what happens past it.** A lock wait counts toward the timeout. Past it, the command goes on detached, and `fetch --wait <log>` gives its rc. A lock wait states its bound.
- **Approval drift names only files whose bytes moved.** The receipt carries raw digests and a hash scheme; a file whose bytes match the receipt is not drift, and a receipt an older harness wrote says so. The byte proof leaves out only plain-scalar `status:` lines, so a status flip is no drift and an aliased one still is.
- **A phase snapshot that does not count yields to a re-verify that does.** First-wins froze a PASS_WITH_RISK-over-red snapshot for good; a counting re-verify now replaces it and the replaced record is appended to `phase-superseded-<phase>.jsonl`. `cook next` names that way out.
- **`cook next --phase P` on a phase that already passed answers `phase_passed`** (exit 0, naming what is ready next) instead of asking for an implementation or a verification that is on disk.
- **An unforced `cook next` leaves a phase another tree claimed to that tree.** A mark taken by `next --phase P` or `prompt developer --phase P` is a claim; the projection hands this tree an unclaimed phase, and with only claimed ones left names one and takes no mark. `ready_alongside` says which phases another tree claimed.
- **The developer delegate is answered in place.** `prompt developer` under `HARNESS_AGENT=developer` no longer tells the delegate to spawn a developer.
- **A `post:` entry naming a snapshot its own verify never writes is refused** (`verification-P2.json` on node `phase-2-x`): plan_graph validate, the plan projection, approval and cook preflight all name it. `cook verify` names the one flag that is missing.
- **A named symbol reaches a path-scoped fact as its module's file** (`mod::sym` or a dotted module), so `--fact-subjects` feeds providers that read paths.
- **pkgsync reads the files the snapshot reads**: git-listed only, vendored and ignored trees skipped, test membership judged from the package's code dir.
- **pkgsync resolves which dist an import comes from out of the repo's `.venv`** — the installed files, longest dotted prefix, so `google.protobuf` and `google.auth` stay apart — with one shared table as fallback (`cv2` is any opencv build). The JSON says where the answer came from (`import_names`).
- **The `tree:` line compares the tracked set, not only the bytes**, and `sync` onto a lane mirrors the local index; a lane whose index differs is named and refused like a stale tree. A dirty local tree is said out loud, with `run --at HEAD` for a base measurement.
- **A lane reinstalls an editable workspace member the sync left without an import hook** (built while its code dir was empty), and names one still without it; `sync` onto a remote with a `.venv` does the same.
- **`sync` ends on the `tree:` line `run` prints** and refuses (rc 3) when the trees still differ; a same-HEAD byte mismatch lists its paths (`differs: path (edited here, at HEAD there)`, `only on the remote`, `deleted here, still there`, …) on `run` too.
- **A run that outlives `--timeout` says it is detached** and names `hs-rops fetch --wait <log>`, which waits for its rc line (or for its process group to vanish) and exits with the run's own rc.
- **`cook verify --from FILE --phase P` cross-checks** the file's phase instead of refusing; a mismatch is named. A missing `--verdict`/`--phase` shows the whole form, as does `needs_implementation`.
- **A phase is judged by its own record.** `cook next --phase P` reads `phase-latest-P.json` before the plan's shared `verification.json`, which parallel phases overwrite; a passed phase answers `phase_passed` from its own record too; and `cook verify` takes the phase it recorded from its own flags, not from a read-back a sibling tree can overwrite.
- **`glossary_register` names every file a call wrote under `commit_together`**; the revision trail is the SSOT's history, not a stray file.
- **hs-code's `measured.dirty` means what git means; `stale` is new.** A snapshot row used `dirty` for "HEAD moved past this snapshot", so a clean tree read dirty. Now `dirty` = uncommitted changes in the measured roots on every row, `stale` = snapshot of another commit. A `--fresh` graph query files its measurement in this worktree's own base and reuses it for identical content (measured: ~25 s every call, now once per content, then under 1 s); `check` verbs still measure into a scratch dir.
- **`graph importers --symbol` counts a use through a module accessor** (`_pkg().purge()`, where `_pkg` imports and returns the module), and keeps an importer that writes `.SYMBOL` on a receiver no import binds as `unresolved_dynamic` with its lines, instead of dropping it as "never uses".
- **An empty graph answer is an answer.** `importers`, `importers --symbol`, `changed` and `unassigned` exit 0 on an empty result with a note naming what was scanned; `where` and `grep` keep exit 1 on no match and gain the same note.
- **Red-team disposition tables per round.** `## Red-team disposition — r2 (security)` counts; a table whose heading names a report covers that report's ids only, so a reused id is not covered by an earlier round's row. A near-miss heading is quoted with its line.
- **A phase's open mark is kept per tree.** A `cook next` read in the main tree stamped that tree's HEAD as the lane's commit-range start; verify and the review gate now read the mark taken in the tree they measure.
- **`--fact-subjects` with a symbol is answered at every step.** A step declaring other facts (cook `needs_implementation`: `code.tests_reached`) dropped `code.callers` without a word; named subjects now read `code.callers` and `code.mentions` on request beside it.
- **A `uv run …` `HARNESS_PYTHON` no longer needs the package index on every call.** Each launcher first asks whether the cache alone can start it (`--offline`, ~50 ms) and runs online only on a miss, so a flaky index no longer stops every harness command.
- **`hs-run cook verify --sha <c>,<c>` names a phase's commits outright.** The open mark is the HEAD of whichever tree first projected the phase, so a phase cooked in another worktree got a range holding other work, and one committed before it was marked got none. Verify now also says when it had to set the mark itself, or reads another tree than the mark's. The review waiver sized a run only to the last phase's oldest commit; it now sizes it to the newest.
- **A subagent's compaction no longer re-asks the main thread's open question.** `SessionStart:compact` fires inside a subagent too, with the main transcript; the resurface nudge now stays silent when the payload names an agent.
- **Lifting a pause keeps the plan's approval; a new pause still re-opens it.** The approval hash leaves `paused`/`paused_reason`/`reopen_when` out of plan-graph.yaml and the record pins the paused set; the gate and `plan next` read one `drift_reason`. A flow-style `{paused: …}` stays raw, so lifting it still reads as drift.
- **`cook next` says when a phase's build record is stale, and `cook record <role> --phase P --supersede` retires it.** Stale: its report is gone, or it predates the current approval. The retiring line is appended; new state `superseded`.
- **`hs-run plan graph` reports every finding `plan_graph.py` prints.** It had dropped `phase-files`, `merger-owned` and `import-edge-conflict`; both now read one list.
- **`hs:plan` runs the commands a phase hands cook to paste as-is.** One that can run on the plan's base is run while planning and its output written beside it; one that waits on an unmerged phase says so. A syntax check passes a wrong interpreter or a wrong count.
- **Cook can hold a phase in place past the declared-file threshold.** `hs-run cook prompt --flags in_place` for one call, or `posture: in_place|subagent` in plan.md (pinned by the approval hash). The reason names what the threshold alone would answer; `record` treats a forced in_place as in place; the delegate nudge reads the same answer; forces that disagree are refused (exit 2).
- **Scaffolded phase files carry the sections the plan reference lists**, including `Related Code Files`, so plan-graph's file-list check reads them instead of skipping the phase.
- **A scaffolded plan or report is dated from its `--id`**, not the run's clock; a non-date id is refused. `--decisions ID,ID` fills plan frontmatter `decisions:`.
- **`hs-rops run --sync`/`--lane` no longer prints the stale-tree refusal before it rebuilds.** The mismatch it is about to repair reads as a `tree:` note ending "rebuilding the lane first"; a plain `run` on a stale tree still refuses with the `!!` advice.
- **Plan-graph phases can declare shared non-file resources.** `resources:` on a subtask (a DB schema, a ledger outside the repo); two unordered phases naming one are a `parallel-conflict`.
- **A disposition cite with no file before it is counted and named** instead of skipped; another plan's file is cited as `plans/<plan>/…:N`.
- **A subagent started below the project root is told the root's memory dir** — Claude Code names one relative to the spawn cwd, which is neither there nor the project's memory.
- **A dev snapshot stamp carries `built_from`** (`git describe` of the checkout), shown in a stamp mismatch and never compared: `same_tool` is the one comparison reuse and drift checks use.
- **Decision records keep their pre-migration id.** `decision_register.py --map-legacy-ids <commit>` stores `legacy_id` (filled for this register from the renumbering commit); a refusal that meets an old id names the ruling it became.
- **The hand-off symbol warning is one line per symbol.**
- **Hand-off checks reach every line a changed signature touches.** `plan next` lists, per target plan, the lines naming a callable a block quotes (`name(`) that no anchor covers, skipping a name used on more than 15 lines.
- **The red-team step carries how far the plan's files reach.** `needs_redteam` reads `code.fan_in` and `code.importers` for the files the plan-graph will modify or delete. The new `facts_advisory` row key keeps a stale or missing code map from moving the step.
- **A red-team report is named by its round.** `hs-run plan prompt red-teamer` fills in `…-red-team-r<N>-plan-review-report.md`; one report per round, its personas named inside.
- **Disposition cites are checked.** Every plan-local `path:N` in the `## Red-team disposition` table is checked for file and range, and one followed by a «quote» by content; `disposition_cites` carries the counts.
- **`plan next` always counts the hand-off anchors it checked.** `handoff_anchors` gives checked (matched / moved / not found), applied, unchecked, blocks and targets, zeros included, so an empty warning list no longer reads the same as "nothing was checked". An item quoted like an anchor under a target line that names no `plans/` path, or one under a target with no quote, is warned on instead of dropped; a `⇒` inside a quote no longer cuts it.
- **Two worktrees of one clone no longer allocate the same decision id.** Each id is also reserved in the clone's git common dir under a shared lock. `plan_graph` names `merger_owned:` as the way out when two parallel phases share the decision register.
- **The stray agent-memory sweep also starts from the cwd the subagent was spawned in.** The dir lands where the subagent started, read from its own transcript; the SubagentStop payload `cwd` is the session's current one (or, on an older host, its launch dir), so a session that moved before the agent stopped left the dir behind.
- **An `applied:` line no longer re-opens an approved plan.** Marking a pasted hand-off block edited the sending plan, so it fell to `approval_invalid` over a bookkeeping line. The stand-alone `applied:` line is now outside the approval hash, like the frontmatter.
- **A pasted hand-off block can be marked `applied:`** so its anchors stop warning; the target plan's approval is still checked.
- **`phase-files:` reads only a phase table's file column.** Symbols, a guarding-test column, `read`/`run` rows and prose beside the table no longer read as owned files.
- **Hand-off targets under a group dir resolve to their plan,** and a target in no plan is named instead of skipped.
- **Empty `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/` dirs below the project root are removed at SubagentStop.** Claude Code places a `memory: project` agent's dir relative to the cwd, so a session standing in a plan dir left them under `plans/`. One holding files is named, not touched.
- **`plan next` checks a plan's hand-off anchors.** An edit addressed to another plan's `:N` with a «quote» of what is there is reported when the quote moved (`now at :M`) or is gone, and every target plan its paste drifted out of approval is named. Warnings only; format in the plan skill's `references/handoff-anchors.md`.
- **`plan record red-teamer` ingests a report already in `reports/` where it is,** instead of copying it under the default persona — the disposition gate counted every finding twice. The red-teamer prompt now names the `verdict:` line and the `id` column the gate reads.
- **The red-teamer runs a plan's env-bound commands on a lane** (`hs-rops run --lane`) instead of reasoning about them from a read-only tree.
- **Shebang scripts are committed executable.** 414 scripts opened with `#!` but were committed 100644, so running one by path answered "permission denied". A test now holds every shebang script outside the tests to the exec bit.
- **`plan_graph.py` compares the two file lists and shows every independent pair.** A phase file's `Related Code Files` and plan-graph's `files_to_*` are compared (advisory `phase-files:` lines), and phases with no path between them in different levels are listed under `also independent across levels`.
- **`verify_install` prints the `ln -s` that puts a missing launcher on PATH.**
- **The phase-decomposition file-ownership rule matches what `plan_graph.py` checks:** only phases that can run together must not share a file.
- **Every finding of a REVISE red-team report needs its own disposition row.** A table full from an earlier round let a later round's REVISE through untouched. The ids in the report's `id`-headed findings table must each have a row in `## Red-team disposition`; `plan next` and `plan_approval.py` name the missing ones.
- **`manual_test.py --anchor --timeout S`.** The anchor ran every probe under a fixed 120 s, and a killed run read "could not be executed". The bound is now the caller's and a timeout says "timed out after N s". The cap is 14400 s: above a two-hour run's own wall, so that wall ends the run rather than the anchor.
- **A red-team report that concludes REVISE holds the plan.** A report on disk cleared the gate whatever it said, so `plan next` called red-team "ready" with HIGH findings open. The report now carries `verdict: PASS|REVISE`; a REVISE stops `plan next` at `needs_redteam_disposition` and makes `plan_approval.py` refuse APPROVED until plan.md's `## Red-team disposition` table has no empty cell. A report without the line is named on the envelope and holds nothing.
- **`hs-rops run -- bash -c 'cd X && cmd'` keeps its `cd`.** Several arguments were joined with bare spaces, so the far shell read `bash -c cd X && cmd` and `cmd` ran at the tree root. Several arguments are now argv, each quoted whole; one argument is still a shell string (pipes, `&&`, a far-side `$VAR`). An alias's extra arguments and `bench` follow the same rule.
- **`--fact-subjects` reads code facts at any step.** Past `needs_planner` the flag was ignored, so a plan revised after research lost `code.callers`/`code.mentions`. Named subjects now fill the domain's facts at every state of plan, cook, fix and review, read-only: state, `next_action` and exit code stay as without the flag, and a stale snapshot reads `unavailable` with its refresh command instead of rerouting.
- **Every hs-code verb that reads a tree says which one.** A top-level `measured: {repo, head, dirty, mode, snapshot, snapshot_commit}` (named like the hs-run code facts), and `measured_trees` when a call reads two (`graph changed`, `change impact`, diffs). Recorded where a snapshot is read or a tree is measured, never per verb.
- **`graph where` says it matches case-insensitively**, and `--case-sensitive` tells a class from a function that differs only in case.
- **"Latest snapshot" orders two commits stamped in the same second by when each was measured**, not by the sha's hex.
- **`hs-rops sync` keeps `.rops.env*` home.** `lane` filtered it and `sync` did not; out it is never shipped (a stale remote copy is removed), back it is never overwritten.
- **A verb's JSON answer reaches stdout once.** The live stderr tee copied it too, so a reader merging the streams read two documents; output that opens with `{` is held and dropped once adopted as the envelope's `data`.
- **`check dist-obligations` with no `obligations:` block says undeclared** (exit 3) and lists the files outside the dists that name most of them, as a block to paste.
- **The declared-branch warning on code facts judges by ancestry.** A work branch cut from the plan's branch holds its tip and is no longer warned about; the warning no longer tells the reader to check out the integration branch.
- **hs-rops names `lane` when the remote dir is missing.** `sync` copies files only, so a gate reading `git ls-files` on a tree it built sees nothing.
- **A paused phase blocks every phase downstream of it.** Edges were bridged around a paused node, so a phase was offered before the one it needs existed. Blocked phases leave the parallel batches with their reason, stay in the completion count, and `cook next` says `phases_blocked` when nothing runnable is left.
- **Registers write only from an SSOT that reads.** On a `decisions.yaml`, `glossary.yaml` or `backlog.yaml` that did not parse, `--render-md`/`render` cut the view to its empty skeleton and `glossary --add` replaced the whole file with one term, all exiting 0. Writers now refuse with `ssot_unreadable` (file, line, parse error), and every refusal exits 3. A legacy `DEC-<n>` the ledger still stores is accepted; `--root` from a linked worktree or under a global install writes that tree's ledger.
- **hs-rops:**
  - `pipefail` reaches the shell that runs the command, so `false | true` fails.
  - Each lane gets its own log dir.
  - `.rops.env` never syncs to a lane.
  - The lane index mirrors the local one.
  - `doctor` backs up a migrated `.rops.env` and names a missing remote dir once.
  - Load is shown per core.
  - The fingerprint is computed in the C locale.
  - `kill N` reads a number as a PGID and no longer matches its own shell.
- **The safety guard reads a downloader only at command position.** `git fetch | sh`, a CLI's `fetch` verb, `| python3 -c '...'`, and a quoted heredoc note that mentions `curl | sh` now pass. `{ curl x; } | sh` and `do curl x; done | sh` now block; before, they slipped through.
- **`scaffold new-dist`/`new-module` write only under `--apply`.** `--target` without `--apply` wrote real files. An inferred dist joins its exemplar's release group and version.
- **cook:**
  - Every verb takes `--plan`.
  - `record` leads to verify.
  - Attest is keyed by plan and phase.
  - A posture with no resolvable plan says so instead of "0 declared files".
  - The prompt context prefers the plan this session opened.
  - Printed `plan_approval.py` lines run as written (absolute path, interpreter).
- **Shipped rules and agents defer commit attribution and the suite command to the target repo.** A brief that limits writes also rules out agent-memory writes; cook reads whether `plans/` is committed from the repo's ignore state.
- **hs-code graph:**
  - The tool-stamp mismatch says what differs and what to do.
  - A snapshot dry run says DRY RUN.
  - Grep snippets centre on the match.
- **`--help` shows the shell flags.** Every `hs-*` CLI declared a help line for each of its own flags (`hs-code --fresh`, `hs-rops --host`, ...) and no help screen printed it. The top-level help and every verb's help now list them under `shell flags:` (`data.shell_flags` in JSON); `hs-run --text` help does too, at every level, naming the domains each engine flag means something in. `--fresh` is described as what it does: it measures the tree on disk, uncommitted files included, for that one call.
- **`graph grep` counts a symlinked file once.** A tracked symlink (`CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md`) was read as its target, so every match counted twice. It is now skipped and named in a warning.
- **A test-tree row names its dist.** `graph where`/`graph grep` rows for a file no unit measures (a test beside `src/`, a dist's own `pyproject.toml`) read `dist: —`; they now carry the workspace dist their path sits in.
- **`graph` query notes reach the envelope.** In JSON mode (the default) a verb's notes and a freshness warning (`--allow-stale`, outside-the-roots drift) were dropped; they now land in `warnings`. The stale refusal says `--fresh` measures the tree on disk for one call and `graph snapshot --apply` moves the default.
- **`graph unit` edges follow module membership.** In and out edges named a module's second dotted segment, so a namespace package split over dists (`vsf.di.<x>`) read `out: [di]`, `in: []` for every dist while `graph importers` listed the real ones. Edges now name the unit a target module is listed under, as full `<root>/<unit>` keys on both sides; imports inside the unit are no edge of it; a target no measured module owns lands in `out_unresolved`.
- **The behavior linter reports a finding once, to the agent, and counts shell edits.** It folded the whole session at every Stop with no memory of what it had said, so one finding repeated every turn on both the human and model channels. It now speaks only when a finding names a new subject (a file, a command, a search root), and its channel is model-only like the other advisories about the agent's own conduct. A Bash command that changes the project (redirect, `tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv` targets via `bash_write_guard`'s parser; a mutating `git` subcommand; a heredoc script that writes) counts as a change: a session working through the shell read "0 edits".
- **`graph importers` and `graph file` see tests no root measures.** The facts read `test_modules` already; the two query verbs did not, so a module only a test imports read "0 importers" and `graph file` on that test found nothing. Both now include them under unit `test`. `graph where` names a `kind: workspace` unit's directory as its `dist` when no payload carries one (it was `—` on every row), and finds symbols defined in those test files; `graph file` lists its `symbols`, not only their count.
- **`--fact-subjects` says where it applies.** Given to `hs-run plan next` at a state that reads no code facts it was dropped silently (`facts {}`); it is now a `warnings` line naming the state that does. With nothing named, the reason names the verb that takes the flag (`hs-run <domain> next`), not the step's own `next_command`.
- **`code.callers` finds calls made through a re-export and reads Python spellings.** A caller importing a name from a package facade (`from pkg import f`, `f` defined in `pkg._impl`) was counted outside the tree: on a 147-dist workspace 781 refs / 3313 caller edges (24% of the index) went missing, sampled 12/12 real. The callers index now follows module-level `from X import n` bindings to the definition (cycle-safe). The fact also accepts `pkg.mod.name`, `pkg.mod.Class.meth` and a unique bare name (a shared bare name is refused naming every candidate); every re-spelling is a `warning` line, and `basis` states the index size.
- **Tests kept beside `src/` are graph nodes.** A workspace root measures `<dist>/src` only, so `tests_<x>/` beside it never reached `code.tests_reached`/`code.importers` (measured on a 147-dist uv workspace: 0 tests reaching a file 190 tests import). The snapshot now measures every test-tree file no root covers into `_index.json` `test_modules` — reverse walks see them; no unit's size or touch counts move (DEC-v-hieubt15-333).
- **`graph drift` enumerates like the snapshot pass** (roots via `discover`, `scan` honored, test trees via the same door): a fresh snapshot was reported drifted with 1069 "new" files.
- **`graph init` on a workspace mixing `src/` and flat dists** writes `import_roots: [<root>/*/src, <root>/*]`; one meta dist without `src/` used to flip every module to `src.<ns>.…`.
- **`check smoke` orphans**: still listed when an import fails (an empty list read as clean); importing a parent package no longer vouches for its whole subtree; modules only tests import are their own class, `test_only`.
- **hs-run facts and `hs-code` read the same "latest" snapshot.** With two snapshots of one commit, the facts engine kept the name order, where a content-key suffix sorts last, and fed `code.tests_reached` a snapshot of a retired descriptor while `hs-code` read the new one. Both now pick through one rule (`codegraph_snapshot_reader. chronological`: name across commits, `measured_at` inside a tie). Snapshots also carry `descriptor_sha`; one measured under another `codemap.yaml` is `stale` to the engine.
- **A snapshot pass that fails leaves the store untouched** — no empty snapshot directory, no daily head swept before the parse.
